description: First 50 seeds only - testing 'starting well' quality

scoring_criteria.9: Perfect native speech in both languages
scoring_criteria.1-2: Marginal, no one would say this

phrases.english: I'm going to learn speaking with you now.
phrases.other: Ich werde jetzt das Sprechen mit dir lernen.
phrases.notes: English awkward - 'learn speaking' is unnatural; should be 'learn to speak'. German is acceptable but slightly formal with 'das Sprechen'.

phrases.english: I was starting to feel okay when I learn last month.
phrases.other: Ich fing an, mich okay zu fühlen, als ich letzten Monat lernte.
phrases.notes: English has tense error: 'when I learn last month' should be 'when I learned/was learning last month'. German is grammatically correct.

phrases.english: looking forward to learning
phrases.other: freue mich darauf zu lernen
phrases.notes: Both natural fragments. German missing subject but acceptable as phrase component. English perfect.

phrases.english: It's useful to start as soon as you can.
phrases.other: Es ist nützlich, so bald wie du kannst anzufangen.
phrases.notes: English is natural. German word order slightly awkward - 'so bald wie möglich anzufangen' or 'sobald du kannst anzufangen' would be more natural.

phrases.english: do you feel tired
phrases.other: fühlst du dich müde
phrases.notes: Both natural. Simple and correct in both languages.

phrases.english: to speak as hard as I can
phrases.other: so gut ich kann sprechen
phrases.notes: English unnatural - you don't 'speak hard'. Should be 'as well as I can' or 'as much as I can'. German 'so gut ich kann' means 'as well as I can', so there's a mismatch.

phrases.english: How long have you been learning English?
phrases.other: Wie lange lernst du schon Englisch?
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural, idiomatic expressions.

phrases.english: I want to speak English.
phrases.other: Ich will Englisch sprechen.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Core learning phrase, natural in both.

phrases.english: He wants to speak English easily.
phrases.other: Er will leicht Englisch sprechen.
phrases.notes: Both acceptable. English 'easily' placement natural. German word order 'leicht Englisch sprechen' slightly less common than 'Englisch leicht sprechen' but acceptable.

phrases.english: How do you feel when other people are here?
phrases.other: Wie fühlst du dich, wenn andere Leute hier sind?
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural question in both.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to be quiet this afternoon.
phrases.other: Er will heute Nachmittag nicht still sein.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct. English slightly unusual context (why wouldn't someone want to be quiet?) but grammatically fine. German natural.

phrases.english: I'd like to try to explain the whole sentence.
phrases.other: Ich würde gerne den ganzen Satz versuchen zu erklären.
phrases.notes: English natural. German word order slightly awkward - 'versuchen, den ganzen Satz zu erklären' would be more natural.

phrases.english: I'm going to speak English soon.
phrases.other: Ich werde bald Englisch sprechen.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural future intention.

phrases.english: She wants to find out
phrases.other: Sie will herausfinden
phrases.notes: Both natural as phrase fragments. Good phrasal verb practice.

phrases.english: Are you going to help me speak English?
phrases.other: Wirst du mir helfen, Englisch zu sprechen?
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural question.

phrases.english: She wants to start to speak with everyone else soon.
phrases.other: Sie will bald anfangen, mit allen anderen zu sprechen.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct. English 'start to speak' slightly formal; 'start speaking' more natural. German good.

phrases.english: English as often as possible
phrases.other: so oft wie möglich Englisch
phrases.notes: Both work as fragments. Natural building blocks for larger sentences.

phrases.english: I'm trying to speak in English.
phrases.other: Ich versuche auf Englisch zu sprechen.
phrases.notes: Both natural. 'In English' and 'auf Englisch' both correct preposition choices.

phrases.english: He wants to start to meet people who speak English.
phrases.other: Er will anfangen, Leute zu treffen, die Englisch sprechen.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct. English slightly wordy ('start to meet' vs 'start meeting') but acceptable.

phrases.english: to say what I mean
phrases.other: sagen was ich meine
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural idiomatic phrase.

phrases.english: I want to think about it carefully at the moment before I start.
phrases.other: Ich will im Moment sorgfältig darüber nachdenken, bevor ich anfange.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct but slightly clunky. 'At the moment' placement in English awkward. German acceptable.

phrases.english: I like feeling as if I'm nearly ready to speak English better as soon as I can.
phrases.other: Ich mag das Gefühl, als wäre ich fast bereit, so bald wie ich kann besser Englisch zu sprechen.
phrases.notes: Both awkward. English sentence is convoluted and unnatural. German similarly clunky with word order issues.

phrases.english: Did you want to learn to speak English better?
phrases.other: Wolltest du besser Englisch sprechen lernen?
phrases.notes: Both natural. Past tense polite question works well in both languages.

phrases.english: I want to speak English before you finish.
phrases.other: Ich will Englisch sprechen, bevor du fertig bist.
phrases.notes: Both natural and grammatically correct.

phrases.english: He wants to try to speak English very well.
phrases.other: Er will versuchen, sehr gut Englisch zu sprechen.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Good sentence structure in both languages.

phrases.english: He doesn't worry if he needs to improve.
phrases.other: Er macht sich keine Sorgen, ob er sich verbessern muss.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct. English slightly unusual phrasing; 'worry about whether' more natural but acceptable.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to show
phrases.other: Er will nicht zeigen
phrases.notes: Both work as fragments. Clear and natural.

phrases.english: not be able to remember
phrases.other: nicht erinnern können
phrases.notes: Both work as fragments. German 'sich erinnern' would be more complete but acceptable for LEGO component.

phrases.english: I'm going to start to speak English soon.
phrases.other: Ich werde bald anfangen, Englisch zu sprechen.
phrases.notes: Both natural. German excellent. English 'start to speak' vs 'start speaking' is minor preference.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to be quiet when I learn.
phrases.other: Er will nicht still sein, wenn ich lerne.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct but contextually odd (unusual scenario). Functional but not remarkable.

phrases.english: I like feeling I'm going to practise speaking English with you all day.
phrases.other: Ich mag das Gefühl, den ganzen Tag mit dir Englisch sprechen zu üben.
phrases.notes: English awkward - 'I like feeling I'm going to' is clunky. German word order somewhat awkward too.

phrases.english: I wanted to show you how to say it.
phrases.other: Ich wollte dir zeigen, wie man es sagt.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural and useful sentence.

phrases.english: Did you want to read the story before you go?
phrases.other: Wolltest du die Geschichte lesen, bevor du gehst?
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural polite question.

phrases.english: as hard as I can
phrases.other: so gut ich kann
phrases.notes: Translation mismatch: 'hard' vs 'gut' (well). 'As hard as I can' = 'so hart wie ich kann' or 'so sehr ich kann'. Different meanings.

phrases.english: remember easily
phrases.other: leicht erinnern
phrases.notes: Both work as fragments. German 'sich leicht erinnern' would be more complete but acceptable.

phrases.english: I'm going to try to practise English with you.
phrases.other: Ich werde versuchen mit dir Englisch zu üben.
phrases.notes: Both natural. English slightly wordy but grammatically correct. German good.

phrases.english: I want to speak English.
phrases.other: Englisch will ich sprechen.
phrases.notes: English perfect. German uses emphatic word order (topicalization) - natural for emphasis but slightly marked.

phrases.english: be able to remember
phrases.other: mich erinnern können
phrases.notes: Both work as fragments. German includes reflexive 'mich' which is good.

phrases.english: to show me something
phrases.other: mir etwas zeigen
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural fragments.

phrases.english: to learn anything
phrases.other: nichts lernen
phrases.notes: Translation error: 'anything' = 'irgendetwas', 'nichts' = 'nothing'. Opposite meanings.

phrases.english: He doesn't want to learn to speak English better.
phrases.other: Er will nicht besser Englisch sprechen lernen.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Clear negation in both languages.

phrases.english: Because I want to meet someone else tomorrow.
phrases.other: Weil ich morgen jemand anders treffen will.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Good subordinate clause with 'weil' in German.

phrases.english: very useful
phrases.other: sehr nützlich
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Simple and natural.

phrases.english: I'm trying to say something in English.
phrases.other: Ich versuche etwas auf Englisch zu sagen.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural and useful sentence.

phrases.english: How long have you been learning to speak better?
phrases.other: Wie lange lernst du schon, besser zu sprechen?
phrases.notes: Both natural. Good present perfect continuous in English matched with German present + schon.

phrases.english: I wanted to start to learn something useful yesterday.
phrases.other: Ich wollte gestern anfangen, etwas Nützliches zu lernen.
phrases.notes: Both grammatically correct. English 'start to learn' vs 'start learning' minor preference. German good.

phrases.english: I wouldn't like to guess what's going to happen tomorrow.
phrases.other: Ich würde nicht gerne raten, was morgen passieren wird.
phrases.notes: Both natural. Good conditional usage in both languages.

phrases.english: I'm looking forward to speaking English better.
phrases.other: Ich freue mich darauf, besser Englisch zu sprechen.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural idiomatic expression.

phrases.english: I'm not sure what the answer is.
phrases.other: Ich bin mir nicht sicher, was die Antwort ist.
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural expression of uncertainty.

phrases.english: I want to learn how to speak with you.
phrases.other: Ich will lernen, wie man mit dir spricht.
phrases.notes: Both natural. German 'wie man spricht' (how one speaks) is idiomatic.

worst_3_phrases.english: I was starting to feel okay when I learn last month.
worst_3_phrases.other: Ich fing an, mich okay zu fühlen, als ich letzten Monat lernte.
worst_3_phrases.reason: Critical tense error in English. 'When I learn last month' is grammatically incorrect - should be 'when I learned' or 'when I was learning'. The German is correct, making this a generation error in the target language.

worst_3_phrases.english: to speak as hard as I can
worst_3_phrases.reason: Semantic mismatch and unnatural English. 'Speak hard' is not natural English - you speak 'well', 'loudly', 'clearly', or 'much', not 'hard'. The German correctly uses 'gut' (well), revealing a translation inconsistency.
Translation error with opposite meanings. 'Anything' = 'irgendetwas' or 'etwas', while 'nichts' = 'nothing'. This is a significant semantic error that would confuse learners.

summary.quality_assessment: Overall quality is GOOD (7.18 average). 80% of phrases score 7 or above, indicating strong natural language in both English and German. The 5 phrases below score 5 represent 10% of the sample and include 2 grammatical errors and 2 semantic mismatches that should be addressed. The 'starting well' test shows generally high quality with specific fixable issues.
